root.name: Benko Gambit: Zaitsev Variation, Nescafe Frappe Attack
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 b5 4. cxb5 a6 5. Nc3 axb5 6. e4 b4 7. Nb5

overview: Black sacrifices the b-pawn for queenside pressure, and in this line White plays 6.e4 b4 7.Nb5 followed by Bf4 or Nf3. Black plays ...d6 and ...g6 and uses the open a- and b-files with a bishop on g7. White keeps the extra pawn and the centre, and Black goes for long-term compensation.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn and hold the centre

black_ideas.idea: Use the open a- and b-files with rooks
Fianchetto and put pressure on the long diagonal

typical_structures.structure: Benko structure with Black queenside pressure

gambit.notes: White can keep the pawn but Black gets long-term pressure.

level.notes: Black must know theory and plans.

character.reason: Black plays a gambit with concrete tactics.

plans.reason: Black fianchettoes and presses on the queenside.
